Safewave Watch Simulator

Built for floors where workers can't carry a phone. Chapter 1 is the watch on its own: join the site Wi-Fi in the watch's settings, open Safewave from the app list, sign in with a pairing code from the dashboard, and see how a floor watch is locked to the app. Chapter 2 slides the real dashboard in beside Safewave for Business on an iPhone (rendered from the app's own code) and the watch. The dashboard is the live Users page at desktop size: zoom in and out, and press the actual buttons.

Guided demo21 steps in two chapters. Chapter 1 sets up the watch: site Wi-Fi, opening the app, the pairing code from the dashboard, the band, kiosk lock. Chapter 2 runs the whole system side by side: Notify on the real dashboard, the alert on the phone and on the watch, a life-safety alert, and what the dashboard shows when the band or the Wi-Fi drops.

Demo controls (not part of the dashboard)

Plays a sound near the watch. Aware on the watch hears it; the dashboard sends nothing.

Exact screensThe dashboard is the real Users page. The phone is an iPhone 15 running Safewave for Business, rendered from the app's own source code. The watch screens are drawn from the watch app's code.
Phone + bandWhere phones are allowed: the Gen 1 band is paired to the worker's phone, and Safewave for Business carries the alerts. The watch is the phone-free follow-on for floors where phones aren't allowed.
When an alert landsThe band buzzes nonstop until the band button is pressed or the alert is acknowledged on the device. On the dashboard the row shows Awaiting, then Acknowledged.
Safewave AwareThe watch listens on its own microphone for fire alarms, sirens, horns and the other sounds the wearer switches on, and buzzes the band when it hears one. Recognition runs on the watch; nothing is recorded or sent anywhere.
Kiosk lockFloor watches are locked to Safewave with Knox: no watch face, no other apps, and the keys only wake the screen.
